pos.personaBrief: Still 65-69% possession (FourFourTwo, B/R) but with a counter-attacking MSN trio (Grantland, Playing for 90), so the ball is kept yet used to launch fast attacks.

pro.personaBrief: More direct than before: long balls, ball fast to the front three, four Liga goals from long passes (Sportskeeda), yet Barca still build from the back.

est.personaBrief: Base 4-3-3 with set roles (SI, B/R), midfield in tight triangles, Messi drifting inside as situational No. 10.

lar.personaBrief: Messi and Neymar stay wide for switches and 1v1 (B/R, Sportskeeda), but Messi cuts inside and full-backs give width when forwards tuck in (SI).

blo.personaBrief: High pressing and quick regains are the usual strategy (Sports Mole, Sportskeeda), with a flat 4-4-2 and deeper block only in the Clasico.

mar.personaBrief: Switched set pieces from zonal to man-marking (B/R Nov 2014), a single-source fact; open play remains space-based.

pla.personaBrief: Luis Enrique imposed a new model on the squad (Fabregas out, Rakitic in) but adapted: sat back and let Madrid have the ball in the Clasico, rotated 23 XIs in 23 games.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic and ambitious treble winner: a more practical, direct team (Grantland), but one that plays to win everywhere and attacks.

sis.personaBrief: Built around the MSN stars who decide games, with a collective block (Xavi quote), yet Enrique benched Messi and rotated everybody.

jog.personaBrief: Technical Barca core (Xavi, Iniesta, Messi) with pace in the front three; they play quicker and more direct but technique still leads.

bas.personaBrief: Mixed: expensive signings (Suarez, Neymar, Rakitic, Bravo) form the core, while Enrique gave minutes to Munir, Sandro, Samper and Ie and eased Xavi out.

lid.personaBrief: Strict boss: fines for lateness (La Libre), benched Messi and Neymar, tension solved on his terms (Catalunya Radio).
